question.:question/problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=2 x y^{2} + 2 x y - 5 x$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x y^{2} + 2 x y - 5 x)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2 x y^{2} + 2 x y - 5 x)\,j \\  & =(2 y^{2} + 2 y - 5)\,i+(4 x y + 2 x)\,j \\ ∇f(1,2) & =(2 (2)^{2} + 2 (2) - 5)\,i+(4 (1) (2) + 2 (1))\,j \\  & =(7)\,i+(10)\,j \\  & =⟨7,10⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,2)\cdot ⟨x-(1),\,y-(2)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨7,10⟩\cdot ⟨x - 1,\,y - 2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
